renameStackWarning: The stack folder is renamed. If the stack is running it is stopped and started again: containers and networks are recreated with the new name. Bind mounts with ./relative paths follow the folder; absolute paths outside the stack folder are not changed.
renameStackVolumesWarning: These named volumes are named after the stack, with the new name Docker would create new empty volumes:
renameStackKeepVolumes: Keep the existing volumes (adds name: <old stack>_<volume> to compose.yaml)
renameStackBindsRewritten: These bind mounts use an absolute path inside the stack folder: they are changed to the equivalent relative path in compose.yaml so they follow the new folder name:
renameStackBindsVariables: These bind mounts use a variable, so Dockge cannot tell whether they point into the stack folder and leaves them as they are. If they do, update them after the rename (relative ./paths always follow the folder):
pickHostPathNoRoots: No browsable folder. Mount the host folders into the Dockge container with the same path on both sides (e.g. /mnt:/mnt:ro) and list them in DOCKGE_BROWSE_ROOTS (default: /mnt).
insertHostPathHint: Pick a host folder and insert its path at the cursor
folderHelp: Use / for sub folders, leave empty for no folder. Folders only exist in Dockge (saved as x-dockge.folder in compose.yaml): the stack does not move on disk.
renameFolderPrompt: New folder path (use / for sub folders, empty = no folder):
noImageUpdates: All images are up to date.
imageUpdateIntervalHelp: Dockge asks the registries if newer images exist for the tags used by your stacks (nothing is downloaded). Use Update on a stack to pull and redeploy. Add x-dockge: { checkUpdates: false } to a compose file to skip it.
bindToIP: Publish this port only on this IP of the host
apiKeysIntro: API keys let scripts and AI assistants manage the stacks of this Dockge instance through the REST API or the MCP endpoint. Only HTTPS requests are accepted.
apiDedicatedPort: The API has its own listener on {0} (DOCKGE_API_PORT / DOCKGE_API_HOSTNAME).
apiAllowHttpWarning: DOCKGE_API_ALLOW_HTTP=true: keys are accepted over plain HTTP and can be intercepted.
apiHttpsRequiredWarning: No TLS certificate and no trusted reverse proxy: every API request will be refused. Set DOCKGE_SSL_KEY / DOCKGE_SSL_CERT, or put Dockge behind an HTTPS reverse proxy and set DOCKGE_TRUST_PROXY.
apiProxyOk: HTTPS through the trusted reverse proxy ({0}).
apiKeyCreated: Copy the key now: it will not be shown again.
apiPermissionWriteWarning: Full control can create, change, delete stacks and run commands in containers: it is equivalent to root access to this host.

moveAcrossInstances: Stacks and folders cannot be moved to another Dockge instance
storageNotZfs: The stacks folder is not on ZFS: nothing changes for the stacks.
storageReady: The stacks folder is a ZFS dataset mounted correctly. Configure the TrueNAS API below to create stacks and volumes as datasets.
storageProblem_stacksFolderNotDataset: The stacks folder is a plain folder inside the dataset {dataset}. Do not create the dataset {stacksFolderDataset} from TrueNAS or with zfs create: it would be mounted over the folder and hide all the stacks.
storageRemedy_stacksFolderNotDataset: To use datasets, move the stacks to a dataset {stacksFolderDataset}: stop the stacks and Dockge, rename the folder, create the dataset, copy the content back, start again.
storageProblem_mountPropagationPrivate: The stacks folder is mounted into Dockge without propagation: datasets mounted on the host after Dockge started are not visible inside Dockge, which would see (and write into) the empty folder under them.
storageRemedy_mountPropagationPrivate: Mount the stacks folder with rslave propagation in the compose file of Dockge, then recreate the Dockge container:
storageLabelMissingInStackHint: At the next deploy Docker creates it as a plain folder, not as a dataset
storageLabelNotVisibleHint: This path is not mounted into Dockge, it cannot be checked
storageLabelOtherStackHint: The data of another stack: the two stacks stay tied, a rollback or deletion of the other one changes it
storageUseRelativeHint: Use {0}: a path relative to the stack folder follows the stack when it is renamed
storagePickerStackHint: Inside the folder of this stack: use a relative path (./name) from that stack instead
storageCanCreate: Stacks and volumes can be created as datasets (TrueNAS user {0}).
storageProblem_truenasNotConfigured: Dockge runs on TrueNAS: configure the TrueNAS API below to create stacks and volumes as datasets.
storageRemedy_truenasNotConfigured: Create an API key for a dedicated TrueNAS user and enter URL, user and key.
storageRemedy_truenasConnection: Check URL, user and API key, and that the user has the DATASET_WRITE role.
storageProblem_truenasCertificate: The certificate of TrueNAS is not trusted: it is self-signed, or it is not the one trusted before.
storageRemedy_truenasCertificate: Compare the fingerprint with the certificate in use in TrueNAS (System → Certificates): if it is the same, trust it.
storageProblem_stacksMountpointMismatch: On the host the dataset {dataset} is mounted at {mountpoint}, but Dockge sees it at {stacksDir}: datasets would be created where Dockge does not expect them.
storageRemedy_stacksMountpointMismatch: Mount the stacks folder into Dockge with the same path on both sides, and set DOCKGE_STACKS_DIR to that path.
storageProblem_aclRestricted: The dataset {dataset} has NFSv4 ACLs with ACL mode Restricted (typical of the SMB preset): new datasets inherit it, chmod fails and many containers crash at start.
storageRemedy_aclRestricted: In TrueNAS set the ACL mode of the stacks dataset to Passthrough (Edit dataset → Advanced options), or use POSIX ACLs.
truenasUrlHint: wss:// (or https://) followed by the address of TrueNAS as seen from the Dockge container. Only encrypted connections: TrueNAS revokes an API key sent in clear text.
truenasApiKeySaved: Saved: leave empty to keep it
truenasRolesHint: Use a dedicated user, not admin: give it a privilege with the roles DATASET_WRITE (create datasets), DATASET_DELETE (delete a stack with its datasets), SNAPSHOT_WRITE and SNAPSHOT_DELETE (snapshots), then create an API key for that user. The key is stored in Dockge and never shown again.
zfsNewStacksAsDatasets: Create new stacks as datasets (default, can be changed for each stack)
zfsMissingVolumesHint: Only for stacks that are datasets. Through the API "ask" means: stop and return the list.
createAsDatasetHint: Dataset {0}: snapshots, properties and volumes as datasets
missingVolumesIntro: These folders of the stack do not exist yet. Docker would create them as plain folders: choose how to create them.
missingVolumesOwnerHint: Suggested from {0}. Leave empty if the image sets the owner by itself (e.g. postgres, mariadb).
missingVolumesNote: The properties of x-dockge.zfs in compose.yaml are applied to the new datasets.
storageLabelMissingAskHint: At the next deploy Dockge asks whether to create it as a dataset or a folder
storageLabelMissingDatasetHint: At the next deploy Dockge creates it as a dataset
storageLabelMissingDirectoryHint: At the next deploy Dockge creates it as a plain folder (setting)
storagePickerThisStackHint: Folder of this stack: it is inserted as ./relative path
otherStackBindsIntro: These volumes point into the folder of another stack:
otherStackBindsLine: belongs to the stack {0}, used by {1}.
otherStackBindsMissing: It does not exist: Docker will create it as a plain folder.
otherStackBindsHint: The two stacks stay tied: deleting or rolling back the other stack changes this data. For data of this stack use ./name. Continue only if it is intended: you will not be asked again for these paths.
applyRecipeIntro: Change these properties of {1} ({0}) to the values written in x-dockge.zfs:
applyRecipeRecordsize: recordsize applies to the data written from now on: existing files keep their record size.
applyRecipeHint: Click to apply the values of x-dockge.zfs to the dataset
pickerStackEmpty: No folders in this stack yet
pickerNewVolumeHint: Inserted as ./name: Docker creates the folder at the next deploy.
pickerNewVolumeHintZfs: Inserted as ./name, type and owner are written in x-dockge.zfs: the dataset is created at the next deploy (cancelling the change leaves nothing behind).
pickerNewVolumeExists: Already exists: choose it from the list
storageProblem_usernsRemap: Docker runs with userns-remap: a UID inside a container is a different UID on the host. Owners entered in Dockge (dialog, x-dockge.zfs) are applied as they are, on the host.
storageRemedy_usernsRemap: Add the offset of the remapping (see /etc/subuid on the host) to the owners, or leave them empty.
pickerRemoteError: TrueNAS API not used for this list ({0}): showing the folders mounted into Dockge. To browse the whole host give the TrueNAS user the FILESYSTEM_ATTRS_READ role.
snapshotStopFirst: Stop the containers during the snapshot (consistent copy of databases; otherwise it is like after a power cut, fine for PostgreSQL and MySQL)
snapshotIncompleteHint: Some datasets of the stack were created after this snapshot: they are not in it and are not rolled back or cloned.
snapshotRollbackHint: Bring the stack back to this snapshot
snapshotCloneHint: New stack with the files and data of this snapshot
snapshotFootnote: Recursive snapshots of the stack dataset: compose.yaml, .env and every volume dataset at the same instant. Periodic snapshots stay with the snapshot tasks of TrueNAS.
snapshotRollbackIntro: The stack is stopped, compose.yaml, .env and the data of every volume go back to this snapshot, then the stack is started again. Changes made after the snapshot are lost.
snapshotRollbackDestroys: This snapshot is not the latest: the newer one is destroyed | This snapshot is not the latest: these {n} newer snapshots are destroyed
snapshotCloneIntro: A new stack is created with the files and the data of this snapshot (ZFS clones, they take no space until they change). It is not started.
snapshotCloneNote: Before starting it, change container_name and the published ports if needed: they would conflict with this stack. While the clone exists the snapshot cannot be deleted.
snapshotDeleteIntro: The snapshot is deleted for all the datasets of the stack. It cannot be undone.
snapshotTypeName: Type the snapshot name to confirm
zfsAutoSnapshot: Snapshot before "Update" (recursive, before the containers are recreated)
zfsAutoSnapshotKeep: Automatic snapshots to keep per stack
zfsDestructiveApi: Allow rollback and deletion of snapshots through the API (REST / MCP)
zfsSnapshotRolesHint: Roles of the TrueNAS user: SNAPSHOT_WRITE to take and list snapshots, SNAPSHOT_DELETE to delete them (and to keep only the last automatic ones). On TrueNAS 25.04 rollback and clone are allowed only to a full administrator: with a limited key Dockge tells how to do them from TrueNAS.
deleteStackDestroy: Delete the stack and all its datasets
deleteStackDestroyWarning: Warning: deleting the stack also destroys every dataset inside it, including the dataset of the stack, with all their snapshots. Make sure you have a backup of the datasets you care about. It cannot be undone.
deleteStackKeep: Remove only the containers and keep the data (the stack stays in the list)
deleteStackTypeName: Type the stack name to confirm
stackStorageIsFolder: The folder of this stack is a plain folder: its volumes cannot be datasets and it has no snapshots.

adoptHint: Move this dataset inside the stack (instant, same pool) and use ./name
